2.text: Bring. Gr. "overweigh thee," (H.) or turn the balance of the judge (C.) against thee, by money, (H.) which sometimes will corrupt kings. It is better, therefore, to avoid all law-suits. W.

4.text: Fire. v. 13. Prov. xxvi. 20. Such contests are full of danger.

5.text: Family. Or "ancestors." They will be accused of having neglected thy education. People generally associate with those of the like dispositions.

13.text: Sinners. Gr. "a sinner, lest thou be burnt in the fire of his flame, when he shall be enraged. H. --- This is not the time for reprehension. C. --- The envoys of Ezechias prudently answered nothing to Rabsaces. S. Jer. in Is. xxxvi. --- Useless correction must be avoided. M.

14.text: Words. Thus the Pharisees attacked our Saviour. Matt. xxii. 15. In popular assemblies it is dangerous, but sometimes requisite to oppose bold declaimers. C. ix. 25.

16.text: Power. Thou must consider the debt as thy own. Prov. vi. 1. C.

20.text: Love. Gr. "keep the word secret. 21) Do no hidden thing before a stranger." H. --- The skilful alone must be consulted. W.

22.text: Evil. Gr. "false kindness." The rest is omitted. H. --- Samson was undone by Dalilia. When Pompey was going on an embassy, he was taken by king Gentius, who wished to extort his secret from him; but he put his finger in the flame of a candle, that he might see that all his attempts would be fruitless. V. Max. iii. 3.
